prompt:
Rewrite the following so it is easier to read. Keep every fact and number.

This retry loop hammers the payment gateway the way a toddler hammers an elevator button. Five attempts at a fixed 200 ms interval means a 2-second outage burns the whole budget before the upstream even recovers, and every client, synchronized by the same deploy, stampedes back in lockstep: a thundering-herd-on-a-timer. Swap in exponential backoff with full jitter (base 100 ms, cap 10 s, per the AWS architecture guidance) and wrap the call in a circuit breaker. The catch block, which currently swallows every exception including 400-series validation errors, should retry only on 429, 503, and connection resets; a malformed request will fail identically on attempt five. Also, the idempotency key header retry logic needs a test: I suspect duplicate charges slip through when the first POST times out but succeeds server-side. Please ticket the metrics gap too.
text:
**Problems with the current retry loop**

- It retries 5 times at a fixed 200 ms interval, like a toddler hammering an elevator button. A 2-second outage uses up the whole retry budget before the upstream recovers.
- Every client, synchronized by the same deploy, retries in lockstep. This creates a thundering herd on a timer.
- The catch block swallows every exception, including 400-series validation errors. A malformed request fails identically on attempt five, so retrying it is pointless.

**Requested changes**

1. Replace the fixed interval with exponential backoff and full jitter (base 100 ms, cap 10 s, per the AWS architecture guidance).
2. Wrap the call in a circuit breaker.
3. Retry only on 429, 503, and connection resets.
4. Add a test for the idempotency key header retry logic. I suspect duplicate charges slip through when the first POST times out but succeeds server-side.
5. Ticket the metrics gap.
